title: Fraud alert queue, June to September 2026

findings.headline: Nearly 9 in 10 alerts are false positives
findings.detail: Only 313 of 3,000 alerts (10.4%) were confirmed fraud, so 89.6% of analyst effort went on alerts that were not fraud. The confirmed rate has stayed between 9.7% and 11.1% each month.

findings.headline: Three rules carry most of the confirmed fraud
findings.detail: Mule account inbound (31.7%, 243 alerts), New device + high amount (21.9%, 556) and Velocity (15.4%, 408) have the highest confirmed rates. Round-amount transfer (0.6%) and Night-time login (1.6%) almost never find fraud.

findings.headline: New device + high amount hit rate is rising
findings.detail: Its monthly confirmed rate went from 18.1% in June to 24.3% in September. This is worth checking, though the monthly groups are smaller than the full 556 alerts.

findings.headline: Low-yield rules take much of the queue
findings.detail: Round-amount transfer and Night-time login are 33.3% of alerts (17.1% plus 16.2%) and 22.3% of handling time (12.2% plus 10.1%). Together they found few confirmed cases, about 0.6% and 1.6% of their alerts.

findings.headline: Larger amounts and longer cases go with more fraud
findings.detail: The top fifth of alerts by amount (above 34,533) has a 19.8% confirmed rate, against 3.7% in the lowest fifth. Cases taking over 15 minutes are 33.3% confirmed, but longer handling may reflect clearer fraud, not the reverse.

next_steps: Review thresholds for Round-amount transfer and Night-time login, testing whether fewer alerts would lose any confirmed fraud.
Prioritise Mule account inbound, New device + high amount and high-value alerts for earliest analyst attention.
Investigate why New device + high amount confirmed rates rose each month, and check analyst differences of 6.0% to 13.1% for case mix.

conclusion: The queue is mostly false positives (89.6%), but the fraud is concentrated: three rules hold about 84% of confirmed cases, while two rules take 22.3% of handling time and find very little. First, test tighter thresholds on Round-amount transfer and Night-time login, checking that no confirmed fraud is lost.
limits: This review shows patterns in one four-month extract and cannot tell why rules perform differently, whether unflagged fraud was missed, or what any change would cost.
